slides.headline: Compilation without *maintenance* is worse than none
slides.subhead: Every AI knowledge system hits this fork. Most builders pick a side. That is the mistake.

slides.headline: Compile at ingest. Fast answers, and it decays.
slides.body: You structure everything upfront. Then your knowledge changes and the compilation does not. You serve stale answers from a system that looks current.
chips: Looks correct until it is not

slides.headline: Derive at search. Flexible, and it does not scale.
slides.body: Re-deriving context on every query is clean in a demo. At production load it is the bottleneck, and the cost lands on the slowest path you have.

slides.headline: Two sources of truth that *disagree*
slides.body: You build a structured layer. The underlying data moves. The compilation does not follow. Now the confident answer is the wrong one, and nothing in the system flags it.

slides.quote: Database as source of truth. Scheduled compilation on top.
slides.subhead: Not compiled at ingest. Not re-derived at every query. Compiled separately, with maintenance built in.

slides.headline: Maintenance is part of the architecture, not a chore
slides.body: Che-brain runs this way: re-index summaries on a cadence, invalidate compiled nodes when source items change, database as SOT with hybrid retrieval on top.

slides.headline: Database first. Compile second. Maintain both.
slides.body: The compiled layer is an optimization you build and keep, not a setup you run once and forget. Which are you running, write-time, query-time, or hybrid?
